payload.report: Patient meets CRPC criteria: castrate testosterone, three consecutive PSA rises with two 50% increases and PSA>2. Inadequate androgen suppression is ruled out; neuroendocrine transformation is unlikely without biopsy. CRPC progression is established with high confidence. Subtype refinement favors biochemical M0 CRPC (0.78), supported by negative pre-operative imaging and good performance status. However, no contemporaneous imaging is available at PSA progression, and expert recommendations for PSMA PET/CT or bone scan/CT mean M1 disease (0.15) cannot be fully excluded. Thus CRPC progression is confirmed, but definitive metastatic staging requires additional imaging.
